summary: AGROSHIFT is a web-based decision-support prototype that helps farmers and agronomists explore crop rotation alternatives. It combines local farm information, NASA POWER environmental data and farmer priorities to compare a reference rotation, a soil-conservation alternative and a climate-adaptation alternative. Users locate their farm, enter available soil and crop information, review climate context, and save or print an explainable plan. The prototype supports Spanish and English. Its aim is to make environmental information easier to use through agronomic support and cooperatives. The limited crop catalog and agronomic assumptions require expert and local validation before operational recommendations.
details:
AGROSHIFT addresses Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data through a web-based crop rotation decision-support prototype.

Users locate a farm on an interactive map and enter area, current crop and available soil, drainage, water and crop-history information. NASA POWER daily data provide regional environmental context with source, dates and units. Users adjust soil conservation, water management, diversification and productive feasibility priorities. The rule-based backend normalizes their weights and compares three rotation sequences, showing criteria, weighted contributions and limitations. Plans are saved locally in the browser and can be recovered, edited, exported as JSON or printed.

The interface uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, Leaflet and OpenStreetMap. The backend uses Python, FastAPI and HTTPX. Spanish and English, light and dark themes and reduced motion are supported. Open-Meteo forecasts and World Bank national indicators appear separately as supplementary context and are not automatically included in rotation scoring.

NASA POWER supplies regional gridded information, not exact parcel measurements. The crop catalog is limited and agronomic assumptions require expert and local validation. Scores are internal comparisons, not probabilities of success, yield predictions or verified economic returns. We propose a future pilot with agronomists, cooperatives and farmers in the San Juan Valley, Dominican Republic, to evaluate usability and validate assumptions. That pilot has not yet been completed.

NASA resources: NASA POWER Daily Point API; T2M, T2M_MIN, T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, GWETTOP and GWETROOT. Missing values are handled, and radiation is converted from MJ/m²/day to kWh/m²/day. GPM IMERG and SMAP are not claimed as separate direct integrations. https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/services/api/

AI disclosure: ChatGPT and Codex assisted with coding, debugging, research, interface design, wording, translation, testing, documentation and pitch preparation. The scoring engine uses explicit rules and is not a trained machine-learning model.

Other references: Open-Meteo https://open-meteo.com/en/docs ; World Bank https://data.worldbank.org/ (AG.LND.AGRI.ZS and AG.LND.ARBL.ZS); OpenStreetMap https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright ; Leaflet https://leafletjs.com/ ; React Leaflet https://react-leaflet.js.org/ ; Next.js https://nextjs.org/ ; React https://react.dev/ ; TypeScript https://www.typescriptlang.org/ ; FastAPI https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/ ; HTTPX https://www.python-httpx.org/ ; FAO https://www.fao.org/land-water/databases-and-software/crop-information/en/ .
